brief_title: A Research Study Investigating How a New Medicine NNC0721-5186 Works in Women Living With Overweight or Obesity
official_title: A First-in-human Dose Study Investigating Safety, Tolerability and Pharmacokinetics of Single Ascending Doses of NNC0721-5186 in Female Participants Living With Overweight or Obesity

primary_outcomes.time_frame: From time of dosing (Day 1) to Day 36

brief_summary: This study is being done to look at the safety and how the body takes up, breaks down and removes NNC0721-5186 in people living with overweight or obesity when compared to placebo. In the first 3 dosing groups, NNC0721-5186 will also be compared with semaglutide, a medicine already approved for weight management. Participants will either get NNC0721-5186, semaglutide, or placebo. Which treatment participants get is decided by chance.

eligibility.criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Female (sex at birth).
2. Age 18 to 55 years (both inclusive) at the time of signing the informed consent.
3. Body Mass Index 25.0 to 39.9 kg/m\^2 (both inclusive) at screening, with overweight due to excess adipose tissue as judged by the investigator.
4. Considered eligible based on the medical history, physical examination and the results of vital signs, electrocardiogram and clinical laboratory tests performed during the screening visit, as judged by the investigator.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Known or suspected hypersensitivity to study intervention(s) or related products.
2. Previous randomisation in this study.
3. More than one rescreening for this study.
4. Female who is pregnant, breast-feeding or intends to become pregnant or is of childbearing potential and not using adequate contraceptive method.
5. Current participation (signed informed consent) in any other interventional clinical study.
6. Exposure to an investigational medicinal product within 30 days or five half-lives of the investigational medicinal product (if known), whichever is longer, before screening.
7. Any disorder, unwillingness or inability which, in the investigator's opinion, might jeopardise participant safety or compliance with the protocol.
8. Glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) greater than or equal to 6.5 percent (48 mmol/mol) at screening.
